assertion.rationale: WHAT THIS RECORD IS ABOUT. F25 put Container Apps Easy Auth in front of launch-ops, control-tower and compliance, so reaching any of the three now requires an Entra sign-in. It did not require a second factor: Easy Auth delegates to whatever the tenant's sign-in policy asks for, and this repository asked for nothing. The two Conditional Access policies the manifest already declared could not close that -- mls-ca-require-mfa-admins is scoped by includeRoles to the admin directory roles and does not cover a normal user opening a dashboard, and both policies are enabledForReportingButNotEnforced, which enforces nothing at all. WHAT THE REPOSITORY NOW DECLARES. A third policy, mls-ca-require-mfa-dashboards: state 'enabled' (not report-only), grantControls OR mfa, conditions.users.includeUsers ['All'], and conditions.applications scoped to exactly the three dashboard app registrations -- never 'All'. App-scoped rather than tenant-wide is both the least-blast-radius choice and the honest one: it enforces MFA exactly where a human signs in to this estate, and nowhere else. The two broad policies stay report-only deliberately: they target All users and All applications, and an enforced All/All grant in an adopter's tenant is a lockout rather than a demo. BREAK GLASS. Every enforced CA policy must exclude at least one emergency-access account, or a misconfiguration locks the tenant's owner out of their own tenant with no recovery path. The manifest declares an mls-break-glass group flagged "breakGlass": true and the enforced policy excludes it. That exclusion is not documentation: (1) Assert-ManifestSchema refuses any manifest whose 'enabled' policy excludes no break-glass-flagged group, targets 'All' applications, or names no application -- so an unsafe enforced policy cannot be authored, let alone applied; (2) Test-BreakGlassReady reads the group before any enforced policy is created or re-enabled and refuses (outcome 'Blocked', per policy, without stopping the rest of the layer) unless it holds a member that is neither one of this manifest's fictional personas nor an on-premises-synced account -- so the FIRST apply necessarily skips the policy, because the group is created empty and a human adds the account (g0-bootstrap.md item 13) before the next replay; (3) V3.3 fails if the group is excluded but empty, or holds only personas or synced accounts, because an exclusion pointing at an empty group only looks like a recovery path. The group's membership is deliberately absent from the manifest -- an emergency-access credential is held by a real human and must never be one of the fictional demo personas (CLAUDE.md rule 4) -- which is why V3.2 exempts it from set equality and V3.3 asserts the stronger property instead. WHY THIS IS A GAP AND NOT CLOSED. 3.5.3 requires multifactor authentication 'for local and network access to PRIVILEGED accounts and for network access to non-privileged accounts'. This estate declares enforcement for the second half only, and for three applications. mls-ca-require-mfa-admins -- the policy that would cover privileged accounts -- remains enabledForReportingButNotEnforced by deliberate design, because enforcing an All-applications grant against directory-role holders in a tenant this repository does not own is the lockout risk the report-only decision exists to avoid. One prong declared, one prong knowingly not enforced: under compliance/README.md's Register vocabulary, CLOSED means no known open finding stands against the control, and this rationale names one. GAP is the honest word. WHAT THIS RECORD DOES NOT CLAIM. It does not claim the control is met. It does not claim anything was observed: NOTHING IN THIS ESTATE HAS EVER BEEN DEPLOYED, no Azure, Entra or Graph call was made to build or test any of this, and the evidence above is repo-static -- it describes what the repository DECLARES. A Conditional Access policy declared in a manifest is not a Conditional Access policy enforced in a tenant; only V3.3, run by the Verifier against a real tenant, could say that, and it has never had a tenant to run against. It does not claim MFA for privileged accounts, for the reason above. It does not claim MFA anywhere outside those three applications: the MCP tool server (bearer token), the Direct Line token endpoint (origin-pinned) and every workload identity authenticate by other means, which are their own controls (3.5.1, 3.5.2) and not this one. It does not rely on Microsoft's tenant-level mandatory-MFA rollout for administrator portals: whatever that does or does not cover in a given tenant, nothing here configures or verifies it, so it evidences nothing. WHY V3.3 IS MAPPED TO NO CONTROL. V3.3 now asserts real enforcement -- and asserts, as part of the same pass condition, that mls-ca-require-mfa-admins is report-only. A green V3.3 therefore proves the non-privileged half and simultaneously proves the privileged half is off. Mapping it to 3.5.3 would let a passing criterion drive this row to the strongest derived status -- the one that means machine-verified AND met, which compliance/lib/MlsCompliance.psm1 reaches only from the criteria branch -- on a requirement half of which is deliberately unenforced. The mapping is therefore still empty, for a reason that is the opposite of the old one: the criterion is no longer evidence that the protection is off, but it is still not evidence of the whole requirement. 3.5.4 (replay-resistant authentication) has NO record at all and stays NOT_ASSESSED: Entra sign-in is replay-resistant because of the OIDC authorization-code flow the platform implements -- single-use codes, nonce, short-lived audience-bound tokens -- which this repository neither configures nor verifies. Claiming it would attribute a platform property to an authored control, and the register has no word for 'the platform does this and we checked nothing', which is exactly what NOT_ASSESSED means.

recommendation: Two things would close this control, and neither is code this task could write. FIRST, the privileged-account half: flip mls-ca-require-mfa-admins to 'enabled' once an adopter has a validated break-glass account and has reviewed its report-only sign-in impact. The apply script already refuses to enable any policy without one, and the manifest's schema check already requires an enforced policy to exclude a break-glass group -- so the change is a one-word manifest edit plus a sponsor decision, deliberately left to the tenant's owner rather than defaulted on. Note that policy also targets includeApplications ['All'], which the schema check refuses for an enforced policy; narrowing its scope, or accepting All with eyes open, is part of that decision. SECOND, the deployment half: run L3 against a real tenant and let the Verifier's V3.3 read back what Entra actually holds. Until then every claim here is repo-static. Also outstanding: no criterion asserts that MFA was actually SATISFIED at a sign-in (a sign-in log query over authenticationRequirement / authenticationDetails), which is the difference between a policy being configured and a second factor having been presented.
